paper_title: High-precision search for dark photon dark matter with the Parkes Pulsar Timing Array
coupling_convention: dimensionless epsilon, where the U(1)_{B-L} gauge coupling strength is epsilon*e (normalized to the electromagnetic coupling e); NOT converted to g_BL = epsilon*e
notes: Paper places 95% credible upper limits on the dimensionless coupling epsilon^2 for U(1)_B and U(1)_{B-L} dark photon dark matter using 14.2-yr PPTA DR2 timing of 26 pulsars over mass range 10^-23.5 to 10^-21 eV. The main results are in Fig. 1 (epsilon^2 vs m_A), with no numerical table provided. Data points here are APPROXIMATE, reconstructed from text statements: PPTA limits improve on the MICROSCOPE WEP bound (epsilon ~ 10^-24.07 for B-L, i.e. epsilon^2 ~ 10^-48.14) by up to two orders of magnitude in epsilon for m_A < 10^-22 eV, crossing the WEP bound around m_A ~ 10^-22 eV, with roughly epsilon proportional to m_A^2 scaling assumed for intermediate masses. Emitted values are epsilon (linear, not epsilon^2), for the U(1)_{B-L} scenario. The paper also constrains U(1)_B (improvement up to m_A < 3x10^-22 eV). Local DM density assumed rho_0 = 0.4 GeV/cm^3.
